questions.stem: What accounts most for the huge declines in tourism in France?

explain.定位:
Safety concerns have been one of the biggest reasons why the country has lost over half a
billion in revenue already in the first six months of 2016.
安全担忧一直是该国在 2016 年前六个月就已损失超过五亿（美元）收入的最大原因之一。
explain.信号:
最高级 biggest 锁定。这句靠最高级信号成为答案句：one of the biggest reasons 里的
biggest 把 safety concerns 抬成了头号原因。录音后面虽也提到 workers' strikes and
heavy floods，但只是 also 补充，没有被抬到最高，所以最主要原因落在带 biggest 的这
句上。
explain.替换:
Safety concerns have been one of the biggest reasons ↔ Safety concerns.
原词加最高级直对
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
Heavy floods. 盗用了录音原词 heavy floods，但原文是用 Besides violence, workers'
strikes and heavy floods are said to have also been why 把它作为 also 补充的次要原
因，而题干问的是 most 最主要原因。听到这个原词就选，正中陷阱。
借用原文：workers' strikes and heavy floods are said to have also been why international tourists
have stayed away
C) 原词陷阱
Bad economy. 借用了录音里反复出现的 economy 一词，但原文 tourism is extremely
important to the French economy 说的是旅游业对经济很重要、是旅游下滑会伤经济，
而不是经济差导致旅游下滑。它把因果方向反了，又靠 economy 这个原词制造熟悉感。
借用原文：tourism is extremely important to the French economy
D) 原词陷阱
Workers' strikes. 同样照搬录音原词 workers' strikes，但和 A 一样出现在 are said to
have also been why 这个 also 补充里，属次要原因，不是被 biggest 抬最高的那个，因
而不是 most 所问。
借用原文：Besides violence, workers' strikes and heavy floods are said to have also been why
international tourists have stayed away

questions.stem: What do we learn from the report about tourism in France?
options: A) It is competitive with its numerous tourist destinations.
B) It provides many job opportunities for French people.
C) It is the biggest concern of the French government.
D) It plays an important role in the nation's economy.

explain.定位:
According to the French government, the country is the No. 1 tourist destination in the world,
and tourism is extremely important to the French economy.
据法国政府称，该国是世界第一旅游目的地，旅游业对法国经济极为重要。
explain.信号:
强调语气定调。这句靠强调语气的信号成为答案句：tourism is extremely important to
the French economy 中的 extremely important 是录音对旅游业的正面定调；下一句
The sector represents roughly 9% of its GDP 又用占 GDP 约 9% 这个数据为这一定调补
了硬证据，两句合起来明确给旅游业的经济地位定了性。
explain.替换:
tourism is extremely important to the French economy ↔
It plays an important role in the nation's economy.
极重要换说成重要角色
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
It is competitive with its numerous tourist destinations. 借用了录音 the No. 1 tourist
destination in the world 里的 tourist destination 一词，但原文说的是法国本身是世界第
一旅游目的地，根本没说它要和众多旅游目的地竞争。competitive、与众多目的地竞争都
是录音没提到的，属凭原词臆造。
借用原文：the country is the No. 1 tourist destination in the world
B) 未提及
It provides many job opportunities for French people. 听上去合理，但录音通篇只谈旅
游业对经济、对 GDP 的重要，没有一句提到 job opportunities 或为法国人提供就业。它
没有盗用原词，纯粹是符合常识的合理联想，原文并未涉及。
C) 原词陷阱
It is the biggest concern of the French government. 盗用了录音 one of the biggest
reasons 里的 biggest，把它嫁接到旅游业头上，说旅游业是法国政府最大的担忧。但原文
biggest 修饰的是下滑原因，政府只是说旅游业 extremely important，从未说它是政府最
大担忧，偷换了 biggest 所指的对象。
借用原文：Safety concerns have been one of the biggest reasons
Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.
1 A small plane with two sick US workers arrived safely in Chile late Wednesday after leaving
Antarctica in a daring rescue mission from a remote South Pole research station. After making a stop for
a few hours at a British station on the edge of Antarctica, the two workers were flown to the
southernmost Chilean city of Punta Arenas. In a chaotic two days of flying, the rescue team flew 3,000
miles round-trip from the British station Rothera to pick up the workers at the US Amundsen-Scott
station at the South Pole. "The two patients aboard will be transported to a medical facility that can
provide a level of care that is not available at Amundsen-Scott," says a spokesperson. Normally planes
don't go to the polar post from February to October because of the dangers of flying in the pitch-dark
and cold. "Antarctica creates a hostile environment," says the operations director for the British Antarctic
Survey. "If you're not careful, it'll come round and bite you."
周三晚间，一架载有两名生病的美国工作人员的小型飞机在离开南极洲的一次大胆救援任务后安全抵达智
利，该救援任务从一个偏远的南极研究站出发。在南极洲边缘的一个英国站点停留数小时后，这两名工作
人员被送往智利最南端城市蓬塔阿雷纳斯。在两天混乱的飞行中，救援队从英国Rothera站往返飞行3000
英里，前往南极点的美国Amundsen-Scott站接回这两名工作人员。一位发言人表示："机上的两名患者
将被送往能够提供Amundsen-Scott站无法提供的医疗护理水平的医疗机构。"通常情况下，由于在漆黑
和寒冷环境中飞行的危险，飞机不会在2月至10月期间前往这个极地站点。英国南极调查局的运营主管表
示："南极洲创造了一个充满敌意的环境。如果你不小心，它会反过来咬你一口。"

questions.stem: What was the small plane's mission to Antarctica?
options: A) To carry out a scientific survey.
B) To establish a new research station.
C) To rescue two sick American workers.
D) To deliver urgent medical supplies.

explain.定位:
A small plane with two sick US workers arrived safely in Chile late Wednesday after leaving
Antarctica in a daring rescue mission from a remote South Pole research station.
一架载着两名生病的美国工作人员的小飞机，于周三深夜从南极一个偏远的南极点科考站执
行一次大胆的救援任务后，安全抵达智利。
explain.信号:
mission 原词点名任务。这句里 a daring rescue mission（一次大胆的救援任务）直接对
应题干问的 mission，是答案信号——录音里出现和题干同根的关键词 mission，并把它和
rescue（救援）、two sick US workers（两名生病的美国工作人员）绑在一起，这句就是
承载答案的那一句。
explain.替换:
rescue mission ↔ To rescue
名词任务转成不定式目的
two sick US workers ↔ two sick American workers
US 与 American 同义替换
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
选项 To carry out a scientific survey. 里的 survey 在录音结尾确实念到了——the British
Antarctic Survey（英国南极调查局），但那是个机构名，不是这趟飞行的任务。听到
survey 就选 A，正是掉进原词陷阱。
借用原文：the British Antarctic Survey
B) 偷换概念
选项 To establish a new research station. 里的 research station 录音多次出现——a
remote South Pole research station，但录音说的是飞机'从'这个已有的站出发去救人，根
本没有'建立新站'(establish) 的意思。选项盗用 research station 这个原词，把'从站出
发'偷换成'建新站'。
借用原文：a remote South Pole research station
D) 原词陷阱
选项 To deliver urgent medical supplies. 里 medical 在录音里出现过——a medical
facility（医疗机构），但录音说的是把病人'送去'医疗机构，不是'运送医疗物资'(deliver
medical supplies)。任务是救人、运的是人不是物资，这是盗用 medical 制造的原词陷
阱。
借用原文：a medical facility

questions.stem: What makes flying to Antarctica dangerous from February to October?
options: B) The heavy snow and fog.

explain.定位:
Normally planes don't go to the polar post from February to October because of the dangers
of flying in the pitch-dark and cold.
通常情况下，二月到十月飞机不去极地站点，因为在漆黑和严寒中飞行很危险。
explain.信号:
因果 because of 后接真原因。答案信号是因果连接词 because of——它后面才是'危险'的
真正原因。录音先说 February to October 不飞，紧跟 because of the dangers of flying
in the pitch-dark and cold，因果词后的 pitch-dark and cold（漆黑与严寒）就是答案。
听因果题，重点永远在 because/because of 之后。
explain.替换:
the pitch-dark and cold ↔ The darkness and cold.
pitch-dark 即 darkness 同义替换
explain.排除:
B) 未提及
选项 The heavy snow and fog.（大雪和雾）听起来很符合'南极很恶劣'的常识，但录音讲
致险原因时只说了 pitch-dark and cold（漆黑与严寒），自始至终没提 snow（雪）或
fog（雾）。这是靠常识脑补、原文未提及的典型陷阱。
C) 原词陷阱
选项 The biting winds.（刺骨寒风）里 biting 和录音结尾 bite you 是同一个词根 bite。
录音那句 it'll come round and bite you 是比喻'南极环境会反咬你一口'，并不是说'有刺骨
的风'，更不是 February to October 致险的原因。听到 bite 就联想到 biting winds 而选
C，正中陷阱。
借用原文：it'll come round and bite you
D) 未提及
选项 The ice all around.（四周都是冰）同样是'南极=冰天雪地'的常识联想，但录音讲致险
原因只说漆黑与严寒，全文没有 ice（冰）这个词，更没把冰和危险挂钩。这是常识脑补、
原文未提及。

questions.stem: How did Rick Rahim remove his son's loose tooth?
options: A) By tying it to a door handle.
B) By shaking it back and forth.
C) With a remote control craft.

explain.定位:
Instead, Mr. Rahim tied one end of a string around his son's tooth and the other end to his
full-sized commercial helicopter.
相反，Rahim 先生把一根绳子的一端系在儿子的牙上，另一端系在他那架全尺寸商用直升
机上。
explain.信号:
转折 Instead 后是真做法。答案句由 Instead 领起。前一句先说他"没有"用系门把手 he
did not waste time by tying it to a door handle 的老办法，Instead 一转，后面才是他
真正的做法——把绳子另一端系到 full-sized commercial helicopter 上。听力里"否定
+Instead/But"之后的内容才是落点。
explain.替换:
full-sized commercial helicopter ↔ a full-sized helicopter
去掉 commercial 的同形保留
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
By tying it to a door handle. 直接盗用了录音里 tying it to a door handle 的原词，但这
句前面有 he did not waste time by tying it to a door handle——是他"没有"采用的老办
法，听到"门把手"就选正好中圈套。
借用原文：he did not waste time by tying it to a door handle
B) 未提及
By shaking it back and forth.（来回摇晃）是生活里另一种拔牙土法，听着合理，但录音
通篇没有任何"摇晃"的表述，属于凭常识脑补的方法。
C) 张冠李戴
With a remote control craft. 与录音结尾 some parents have used remote control
helicopters to pull teeth before 的"remote control"撞词，但那是"别的父母"以前用遥控
机干的事，不是 Rahim 这次的做法，混淆了"谁用、用的是真机还是遥控机"。
借用原文：some parents have used remote control helicopters to pull teeth before

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Rick Rahim?
options: A) He has lots of fans on Facebook.
B) He has rich experience in flying.
C) He often suffers from toothaches.
D) He has learned to pull teeth from a video.

explain.定位:
At the end of the video, Mr. Rahim assures watchers that the circumstances were safe, and
that he has 13 years of helicopter flying experience behind him.
在视频结尾，Rahim 先生向观众保证当时情况是安全的，而且他已有 13 年的直升机飞行
经验。
explain.信号:
具体年数佐证经验。答案信号是一个被点明的具体数字 13 years of helicopter flying
experience。新闻里凡给出确切年数/数据，往往就是某道细节题的命中点；这里"13 年飞
行经验"正是对"飞行经验丰富"的实证。
explain.替换:
13 years of helicopter flying experience ↔ rich experience in flying
具体年数概括为丰富
explain.排除:
A) 原词陷阱
He has lots of fans on Facebook. 借用了录音里 posted a video clip of his playful
venture on Facebook 的"Facebook"，但原文只说他在 Facebook 上"发了视频"，从没说
他"粉丝众多"，是拿真实平台名脑补出的结论。
借用原文：posted a video clip of his playful venture on Facebook
C) 张冠李戴
He often suffers from toothaches. 蹭了全篇"tooth/牙"的话题词，但录音里松动的是 his
seven-year-old son's tooth——儿子的牙，不是他常牙疼，把对象从儿子张冠李戴到了他
本人。
借用原文：his seven-year-old son's tooth
D) 与原文相反
He has learned to pull teeth from a video. 把录音里的"video"原词拿来，却倒置了关
系：原文是他自己 posted a video clip（发布视频），并非"从视频里学拔牙"，方向正好反
了。
借用原文：posted a video clip of his playful venture on Facebook

questions.stem: What did Rick Rahim advise parents to do with their kids?
options: C) Do something fun and creative.
D) Play with them in a safe place.

explain.定位:
The father of four posted a video clip of his playful venture on Facebook, advising parents to
do fun and creative stuff with their kids.
这位四个孩子的父亲在 Facebook 上发布了这段顽皮冒险的视频，建议父母和孩子一起做有
趣又有创意的事。
explain.信号:
建议词 advising 直引。答案信号就是建议动词 advising parents to do——题干问
advise，录音用 advising 直接呼应，紧跟其后的 fun and creative stuff with their kids 就
是他建议的内容，几乎是题干与原文逐词对应。
explain.替换:
do fun and creative stuff with their kids ↔ Do something fun and creative.
stuff 换成 something
explain.排除:
A) 未提及
Spend more time together.（多花时间相处）听起来是很正常的育儿建议，但录音里他建
议的是"做有趣有创意的事"，从没说"多陪伴/多花时间"，是凭常识替他补的话。
B) 偷换概念
Tell them adventure stories. 蹭了录音里 playful venture（顽皮冒险）的"冒险"色彩，但
原文 venture 指他"拔牙这桩冒险行为"，不是让父母"给孩子讲冒险故事"，把"做冒险事"偷
换成了"讲冒险故事"。
借用原文：posted a video clip of his playful venture on Facebook
D) 张冠李戴
Play with them in a safe place. 借用了录音反复强调的"safe"——但 the circumstances
were safe 是他在说"自己当时做得安全"，不是建议父母"在安全的地方陪孩子玩"，把"他自
述安全"嫁接成了"对父母的建议"。
借用原文：Mr. Rahim assures watchers that the circumstances were safe

questions.stem: Why is the man making the phone call?
options: A) To confirm an urgent appointment.
B) To collect a package from the woman.
C) To ask the woman to sign a document.
D) To arrange the delivery of a package.

explain.定位:
Hi, Emma. I'm Paul from Hennes Delivery Service. Here is a package for you. Are you at
home to collect it?
你好，Emma。我是 Hennes 快递公司的 Paul。这里有一个你的包裹。你在家可以收
件吗？
explain.信号:
开场自报来意。男方一开口就 I'm Paul from Hennes Delivery Service. Here is a
package for you.，先报公司身份、再说"有你一个包裹"——这种"自报家门 + 直陈事由"的
开场白就是目的题的答案信号，紧接着的 Are you at home to collect it? 更点明是来约送
件的。
explain.替换:
Here is a package for you. Are you at home to collect it? ↔ To arrange the delivery of a package
送件具体化为安排配送
explain.排除:
B) 与原文相反
To collect a package from the woman. 把方向搞反了：录音里 collect 的是女方收件
（Are you at home to collect it? 指她来收），不是男方从女方处取件。盗用了原文的
collect 和 package，却把"谁收谁的件"颠倒了。
借用原文：Are you at home to collect it?
C) 原词陷阱
To ask the woman to sign a document. 盗用了后文 it needs a signature 和 sign the
form 里的"签字"，但签字只是收件时的一个环节，不是"打这通电话"的目的。听到 sign 就
选，正中原词陷阱。
借用原文：it needs a signature to confirm you have received it
A) 未提及
To confirm an urgent appointment. 里的"紧急约会"录音通篇没提，全程只在谈送货时
间，没有任何"urgent/appointment"。属于凭空编造的干扰。

questions.stem: Why can't the woman meet the man today?
options: B) She is visiting a friend.
C) She is not at home.
D) She is not feeling well.

explain.定位:
Oh, sorry, Paul. I'm out at the moment.
哦，抱歉，Paul，我现在不在家（出门在外）。
explain.信号:
被问者直接应答。男方问 Are you at home to collect it?，女方紧接着 I'm out at the
moment 作答——这句"被问者对问题的直接回应"就是答案信号，她为何今天见不了，全
在这句。
explain.替换:
I'm out at the moment ↔ She is not at home
出门在外＝不在家
explain.排除:
A) 过度推断
She is doing shopping. 听着能解释"出门"，但录音只说 I'm out at the moment，从没说
她在购物。是给"出门"硬安一个具体去向的编造项。
B) 张冠李戴
She is visiting a friend. 盗用了后文 I have a friend coming around in the afternoon，
但那是"后天下午有朋友来她家"，既不是今天、也不是她去访友。把后天的朋友安到"今天为
什么不行"上，是张冠李戴。
借用原文：I have a friend coming around in the afternoon
D) 未提及
She is not feeling well. 录音通篇没提她生病或不舒服，她说的只是"出门在外"。属凭空添
加的状态。

questions.stem: Why is the man unable to see the woman tomorrow?
options: A) He will be off duty the whole day.
B) He will be working somewhere else.
C) He will have to have his car repaired.
D) He will be too busy to spare any time.

explain.定位:
I won't be in the area tomorrow as I have some other deliveries to make on the other side
of town.
我明天不在这片区域，因为我要去城另一头送别的件。
explain.信号:
因果 as 引出原因。女方提了明天上午的时间后，男方答 I won't be in the area tomorrow
as I have some other deliveries to make——这里的 as 是因果信号词，as 后面那句"去
城另一头送别的件"才是他明天来不了的真正原因，正是答案落点。
explain.替换:
I have some other deliveries to make on the other side of town ↔
He will be working somewhere else
去别处送件＝在别处工作
explain.排除:
A) 与原文相反
He will be off duty the whole day. 说他"整天休息"，恰恰反了——录音里他明天满是
other deliveries to make，是忙着干活、不是休假。极性正好相反。
借用原文：I have some other deliveries to make
C) 未提及
He will have to have his car repaired. 录音从没提修车，他不来的原因是"去别处送件"。
属无中生有。
D) 偷换概念
He will be too busy to spare any time. 和正确项意思贴得近，但他给的理由是"人在城另
一头"（地点不在），不是"忙到抽不出空"。录音强调的是 I won't be in the area（不在本
区），重点在"地点"而非"太忙"，选它就把具体原因换成了笼统的"忙"。
借用原文：I won't be in the area tomorrow

questions.stem: What should the woman do to receive her purchase?

explain.定位:
So you just need to sign the form to say you've received it.
所以你只需要在表格上签个字，确认你已经收到了。
explain.信号:
结尾 you just need to 给要求。对话临收尾时男方说 you just need to sign the form
——"you just need to"（你只需要）是典型的"交代要求"信号，正面回答了"领件该做什
么"，是本题答案句。
explain.替换:
sign the form to say you've received it ↔ Sign her name
签表格＝签名
explain.排除:
B) 原词陷阱
Confirm online. 蹭了录音里 you paid for it when you ordered it online 的 online，但
那是说她"网上下单付过钱"，不是领件要"线上确认"。盗用 online 一词答非所问。
借用原文：you paid for it when you ordered it online
C) 原词陷阱

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about Mount Etna?
options: A) It has kept growing over the centuries.

However, its height often changes when volcanic material accumulates during eruptions and
subsequently collapses.

explain.信号:
转折 However 后才是真意。这句以 However 起头，前一句刚说它是欧洲最高的活火山，

its height often changes when volcanic material accumulates during eruptions ↔
Its height changes with each volcanic eruption
同义改写：喷发时堆积坍塌＝随喷发而变

A) 与原文相反

questions.stem: Unemployed young men are more likely to live with their parents than the employed.
questions.passage:
Living with parents edges out other living arrangements for 18- to 34-year-olds

A) Broad demographic(人口的) shifts in marital status, educational attainment and employment have transformed the way young adults in the U.S. are living, and a new Pew Research Center analysis highlights the implications of these changes for the most basic element of their lives—where they call home. In 2014, for the first time in more than 130 years, adults aged 18 to 34 were slightly more likely to be living in their parents' home than they were to be living with a spouse or partner in their own household.

B) This turn of events is fueled primarily by the dramatic drop in the share of young Americans who are choosing to settle down romantically before age 35. Dating back to 1880, the most common living arrangement among young adults has been living with a romantic partner, whether a spouse or a significant other. This type of arrangement peaked around 1960, when 62% of the nation's 18- to 34-year-olds were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, and only one-in-five were living with their parents.

C) By 2014, 31.6% of young adults were living with a spouse or partner in their own household, below the share living in the home of their parent(s) (32.1%). Some 14% of young adults lived alone, were a single parent or lived with one or more roommates. The remaining 22% lived in the home of another family member (such as a grandparent, in-law or sibling(兄弟姐妹)), a non-relative, or in group quarters like college dormitories.

D) It's worth noting that the overall share of young adults living with their parents was not at a record high in 2014. This arrangement peaked around 1940, when about 35% of the nation's 18- to 34-year-olds lived with mom and/or dad (compared with 32% in 2014). What has changed, instead, is the relative share adopting different ways of living in early adulthood, with the decline of romantic coupling pushing living at home to the top of a much less uniform list of living arrangements.

E) Among young adults, living arrangements differ significantly by gender. For men aged 18 to 34, living at home with mom and/or dad has been the dominant living arrangement since 2009. In 2014, 28% of young men were living with a spouse or partner in their own home, while 35% were living in the home of their parent(s). Young women, however, are still more likely to be living with a spouse or romantic partner (35%) than they are to be living with their parent(s) (29%).

F) In 2014, more young women (16%) than young men (13%) were heading up a household without a spouse or partner. This is mainly because women are more likely than men to be single parents living with their children. For their part, young men (25%) are more likely than young women (19%) to be living in the home of another family member, a non-relative or in some type of group quarters.

G) A variety of factors contribute to the long-run increase in the share of young adults living with their parents. The first is the postponement of, if not retreat from, marriage. The average age of first marriage has risen steadily for decades. In addition, a growing share of young adults may be avoiding marriage altogether. A previous Pew Research Center analysis projected that as many as one-in-four of today's young adults may never marry. While cohabitation(同居) has been on the rise, the overall share of young adults either married or living with an unmarried partner has substantially fallen since 1990.

H) In addition, trends in both employment status and wages have likely contributed to the growing share of young adults who are living in the home of their parent(s), and this is especially true of young men. Employed young men are much less likely to live at home than young men without a job, and employment among young men has fallen significantly in recent decades. The share of young men with jobs peaked around 1960 at 84%. In 2014, only 71% of 18- to 34-year-old men were employed. Similarly with earnings, young men's wages (after adjusting for inflation) have been on a downward trajectory(轨迹) since 1970 and fell significantly from 2000 to 2010. As wages have fallen, the share of young men living in the home of their parent(s) has risen.

I) Economic factors seem to explain less of why young adult women are increasingly likely to live at home. Generally, young women have had growing success in the paid labor market since 1960 and hence might increasingly be expected to be able to afford to live independently of their parents. For women, delayed marriage—which is related, in part, to labor market outcomes for men—may explain more of the increase in their living in the family home.

J) The Great Recession (and modest recovery) has also been associated with an increase in young adults living at home. Initially in the wake of the recession, college enrollments expanded, boosting the ranks of young adults living at home. And given the weak job opportunities facing young adults, living at home was part of the private safety net helping young adults to weather the economic storm.

K) Beyond gender, young adults living arrangements differ considerably by education—which is tied to financial means. For young adults without a bachelor's degree, as of 2008 living at home with their parents was more prevalent than living with a romantic partner. By 2014, 36% of 18- to 34-year-olds who had not completed a bachelor's degree were living with their parent(s) while 27% were living with a spouse or partner. Among college graduates, in 2014 46% were married or living with a partner, and only 19% were living with their parent(s). Young adults with a college degree have fared much better in the labor market than their less-educated counterparts, which has in turn made it easier to establish their own households.

questions.stem: What do most Americans think of women leaders according to a new Pew Research Center survey?
options: A) They have to do more to distinguish themselves.
B) They have to strive harder to win their positions.
C) They are stronger than men in terms of willpower.
D) They are just as intelligent and innovative as men.
questions.passage:
According to the majority of Americans, women are every bit as capable of being good political leaders as men. The same can be said of their ability to dominate the corporate boardroom. And according to a new Pew Research Center survey on women and leadership, most Americans find women indistinguishable from men on key leadership traits such as intelligence and capacity for innovation, with many saying they're stronger than men in terms of being passionate and organized leaders.

So why, then, are women in short supply at the top of government and business in the United States? According to the public, at least, it's not that they lack toughness, management talent or proper skill sets.

It's also not all about work-life balance. Although economic research and previous survey findings have shown that career interruptions related to motherhood may make it harder for women to advance in their careers and compete for top executive jobs, relatively few adults in the recent survey point to this as a key barrier for women seeking leadership roles. Only about one-in-five say women's family responsibilities are a major reason why there aren't more females in top leadership positions in business and politics.

Instead, topping the list of reasons, about four-in-ten Americans point to a double standard for women seeking to climb to the highest levels of either politics or business, where they have to do more than their male counterparts to prove themselves. Similar shares say the electorate(选民) and corporate America are just not ready to put more women in top leadership positions.

As a result, the public is divided about whether the imbalance in corporate America will change in the foreseeable future, even though women have made major advances in the workplace. While 53% believe men will continue to hold more top executive positions in business in the future, 44% say it's only a matter of time before as many women are in top executive positions as men. Americans are less doubtful when it comes to politics: 73% expect to see a female president in their lifetime.

questions.stem: What does the global study tell us about people's height in the last hundred years?
options: A) There is a remarkable difference across continents.
B) There has been a marked increase in most countries.
C) The increase in people's height has been quickening.
D) The increase in women's height is bigger than in men's.
questions.passage:
People have grown taller over the last century, with South Korean women shooting up by more than 20cm on average, and Iranian men gaining 16.5cm. A global study looked at the average height of 18-year-olds in 200 countries between 1914 and 2014.

The results reveal that while Swedes were the tallest people in the world in 1914, Dutch men have risen from 12th place to claim top spot with an average height of 182.5cm. Latvian women, meanwhile, rose from 28th place in 1914 to become the tallest in the world a century later, with an average height of 169.8cm.

James Bentham, a co-author of the research from Imperial College, London, says the global trend is likely to be due primarily to improvements in nutrition and healthcare. "An individual's genetics has a big influence on their height, but once you average over whole populations, genetics plays a less key role," he added.

A little extra height brings a number of advantages, says Elio Riboli of Imperial College. "Being taller is associated with longer life expectancy," he said. "This is largely due to a lower risk of dying of cardiovascular(心血管的) disease among taller people."

But while height has increased around the world, the trend in many countries of north and sub-Saharan Africa causes concern, says Riboli. While height increased in Uganda and Niger during the early 20th century, the trend has reversed in recent years, with height decreasing among 18-year-olds.

"One reason for these decreases in height is the economic situation in the 1980s," said Alexander Moradi of the University of Sussex. The nutritional and health crises that followed the policy of structural adjustment, he says, led to many children and teenagers failing to reach their full potential in terms of height.

Bentham believes the global trend of increasing height has important implications. "How tall we are now is strongly influenced by the environment we grew up in," he said. "If we give children the best possible start in life now, they will be healthier and more productive for decades to come."
